liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Althea** (1 review): The song is described as beautiful, marking its first full-bodied era in 1981 [22]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Garcia's middle solo is particularly triumphant in this hot version [28]
- **China Cat Sunflower I Know You Rider** (1 review): A dynamic performance closes out the first set [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.5241.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 180 min [1]
- **gd1981-05-12.139954.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 168 min [2]
- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.chasingwilma.118987.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 180 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: The song is dedicated to Bob Marley, featuring a fantastic performance [30]
- **gd1981-05-12.149199.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1981-05-12.153022.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 173 min [7]
- **gd1981-05-12.mtx.seamons.99045.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 169 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [9]. Said about its sound: The performance is very emotional, with well-done vocals from Bob [25]
- **gd1981-05-12.123259.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [10]. Said about its sound: The song is dedicated to Bob Marley, opening a well-played second set [27]
- **gd81-05-12.sbd.jeffm.1664.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [17]. Said about its sound: Jerry's slide playing sounds grating as he runs out of ideas; Brent's keyboard setting detracts from an otherwise decent performance [23]

## Around the show

- Weir dedicates the song to Bob Marley during the performance [21]
- The band plays several teases of Lively Up Yourself during the jam [21]
- The band responds to losing two Bobs in one week with passionate playing [26]
- Weir offers heartfelt words for Bob Marley before the Don't Ease Me In encore [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.5241.shnf**: taped by DAE(EAC) and SHN Encoding by Jeff M.; transferred by Upload and Tracking/SHN Encoding of d1t01,t02,t10 & t11 by; source: SBD>Master Cassette>Cassette>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd1981-05-12.139954.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (TDK MA90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) >… [2]
- **gd1981-05-12.sbd.chasingwilma.118987.flac16**: taped by chasingwilma; transferred by chasingwilma; source: Sbd> D-5> MC [4]
- **gd1981-05-12.149199.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM700 mics > Sony TC-D5M [5]
- **gd1981-05-12.153022.nak500.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi DM-500 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII) [7]
- **gd1981-05-12.mtx.seamons.99045.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [9]. Also: Jeff M. transferred the SBD, and JR Fishman handled the AUD transfer and encoding [9]
- **gd1981-05-12.123259.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [10]
- **gd81-05-12.sbd.jeffm.1664.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [17]
